summary: A first-person account of the Annual Charity Fun Run, a 5K held on September 10, 2023 starting at Central Park, to raise funds for the local children's hospital. The narrator describes the diverse crowd, Mayor Helen Ramirez's opening speech, the route with cheer stations, volunteers, post-race festivities, and sponsor acknowledgments. The piece emphasizes community unity and the promise to continue the tradition next year.
one_line: A personal recap of the September 10, 2023 Annual Charity Fun Run 5K, which raised funds for the local children's hospital and showcased community spirit.
key_facts: The Annual Charity Fun Run was held on September 10, 2023, on a crisp September morning.
The run started at Central Park, the official starting point, and began at precisely 8:00 AM.
Mayor Helen Ramirez opened the event with a speech and called "On your marks, get set, go!"
Proceeds from the run help fund the local children's hospital.
The 5K route passed through the park, the historic downtown with cobblestone streets, and a riverside path.
The local band The Harmonics played an impromptu set at the halfway mark.
At mile one, the Thompson family ran a lemonade stand with children cheering with handmade signs.
At mile two, the high school cheer squad performed acrobatics for the runners.
Michael, a retired veteran, was among the volunteers and had volunteered for as long as anyone could remember.
Post-race festivities included free treats from local food vendors, free health check-ups at health-focused booths, and games in the park.
Checks were presented to the beneficiaries after the race.
Sponsors InnovaTech (a local tech company) and Greenfields Market (a family-owned grocery chain) were especially commended for substantial contributions.
Participants included Greg from the local bakery and little Sara with her father, and ages ranged from toddlers to septuagenarians.
